title: factdiff.py anchor --quotes takes one quote per fact line, so a DOC fact citing two non-Microsoft sources can anchor only one of them by quote
goal: A DOC fact citing two copy- or quote-reuse sources can be anchored by quote against each: --quotes accepts a quote per fact line and source (or several quotes per line, each matched to the source that holds it), so both anchor rows end located and lint stops warning that the added source's page holds no passage.

run:
import subprocess,sys,tempfile,pathlib;d=tempfile.mkdtemp();p=pathlib.Path(d,'q.csv');p.write_text('line,source,quote
23,S-xc5uusz2,An SVID is not itself a document type.
23,S-yp5feoc6,The X.509-SVID and JWT-SVID profiles are mandatory and MUST be supported by SPIFFE implementations.
',encoding='utf-8');sys.exit(subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/factdiff.py','anchor','--file','auth/spiffe-workload-identity.md','--quotes',str(p),'--dry-run']).returncode)

notes: Plan amendment 2026-10-15: repro reworded to the line,source,quote form that ST-duwzvvq7's gate g1 decided (an optional source column; two-column files read as before), one row per cited source of auth/spiffe-workload-identity.md:23 (S-xc5uusz2, S-yp5feoc6); the earlier two-column repro quoted line 23 twice and could never pass under g1. The repro runs anchor --dry-run, which fetches the two pages.
